reason: Radioactive heating can melt or alter a rocky planetesimal, advancing the goal of exposing its stone and metal.
expectation: The rocky bodies will heat internally, potentially allowing metal and rock to separate.

effect: The rocky planetesimal has melted, making separation of its materials the next plausible step.
reaction: The distinction that not all asteroids melt is useful.
reason: Gravity can separate dense metal from lighter rock within the molten body.
expectation: Metal will sink and rock will form an outer layer.

effect: The molten body has differentiated into a metal core and silicate material; collisions may expose both.
reaction: It is interesting that differentiation can happen before Earth finishes growing.
reason: Collisions between small bodies could break the differentiated world and expose its interior.

choice.combine: A small world with a metal core

expectation: The collision will expose stone and metal from the differentiated body.

effect: The collision exposed core metal, but the stone-and-metal goal has not yet been reported complete.
reaction: The connection to iron meteorites is useful.
reason: Radioactive heating could melt ice inside an icy planetesimal, enabling water to alter its rock.
expectation: The icy body will warm internally, potentially producing liquid water.

effect: Internal heating produced liquid water inside the icy body, making water–rock alteration plausible.
reaction: A frozen exterior concealing liquid water is interesting.
reason: Silicate grains provide rock for the liquid water to alter.

choice.combine: Liquid water inside an icy body

expectation: Water will react with the silicate material, leaving water bound in altered rock.

effect: Water reacted with silicates to form hydrated rock, completing the water-bearing rock goal. The stone-and-metal goal remains.
reaction: It is useful to learn that hydrated minerals can carry hydrogen even after exposed ice disappears.
reason: The exposed core fragments may have a partner that helps complete the remaining goal, but the next combination is unclear.
expectation: Inspection will reveal what can combine with the exposed core fragments.

effect: The core fragments have no available combinations, so the remaining goal likely requires a separate route to exposed stone.
reaction: The inspection ruled out the most obvious follow-up.
reason: Collisions could also break undifferentiated rocky planetesimals and expose their stone.
expectation: The collision will produce rocky fragments that complement the exposed core metal.

effect: Rocky planetesimals have no available combinations, so they cannot provide the missing stone directly.
reaction: That rules out the straightforward collision route.
reason: The differentiated world may have another available operation that exposes its rocky layers.

choice.inspect: A small world with a metal core

expectation: Inspection will show whether the differentiated world can expose stone as well as core metal.

effect: The differentiated asteroid cooled and solidified, providing a rocky exterior that collisions may expose.
reaction: Cooling before breaking the rocky exterior makes sense.
reason: A collision can break the cooled asteroid and expose its stone.
expectation: The collision will produce rocky fragments and complete the remaining goal.

effect: The collision exposed fragments of the asteroid’s rocky layers and completed the remaining goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to expose both the rocky layers and the metal core after finding the cooling step.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making water-bearing asteroid rock was most worthwhile: it showed how hydrated minerals can carry hydrogen even after exposed ice is gone.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the core fragments was less useful because they had no available combinations, though it ruled out a plausible follow-up.

surprise.text: I did not expect the differentiated asteroid to need cooling before its rocky layers could be exposed; inspecting it revealed and automatically performed that step.

arbitrary.text: The need to cool the differentiated body before exposing its rocky layers was not initially clear, although the solidification explanation made sense afterward.

continue.text: I would continue: the chapter connected plausible combinations to useful distinctions about asteroid interiors and water-bearing minerals, despite a little uncertainty about the cooling sequence.
